text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the shooting pain when eating and the history of bilateral infections, are you experiencing any referred pain or a sensation of fullness in your throat?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia (likely secondary to post-tympanoplasty scarring or nerve irritation).

This diagnosis is based on your history of bilateral ear infections, the specific "shooting" nature of the pain triggered by chewing/eating, and the discomfort with earrings (suggesting tragal/cutaneous nerve involvement), which is inconsistent with tuberculosis.
